finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL after only a substring check for "example.io". The check is trivially bypassed, so the server can be made to request arbitrary internal or external hosts and return the response body (full-read SSRF).
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied back to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation; it matches anywhere in the string, including the path, query, fragment or userinfo
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects, with no scheme or host restriction
the response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Only the substring check at main.go:32. There is no URL parsing, no hostname or scheme allowlist, no IP or private-range blocking, and no redirect restriction. Example bypass: /logo?logo=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io. Also bypassed by http://evil.com/example.io, http://example.io@127.0.0.1/ or http://example.io.evil.com/.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a strings.Contains substring check at main.go:32; the strict hostname allowlist at main.go:20 is in the separate /cdn handler, not /logo)
verdict.reason: main.go:31 reads the attacker-controlled `logo` form value, main.go:32 only does a substring match for "example.io" (bypassable via query, path or userinfo), and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and streams the body back at main.go:38.
